WITH base AS (
 SELECT COALESCE(s.SECTOR,'Unmapped') sector, b.SNAP_DT, b.FACILITY_ID, b.DRAWN_AMT, f.COMMIT_AMT
 FROM BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY b
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY f ON f.FACILITY_ID=b.FACILITY_ID
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.CORE.CLIENT c ON c.CIF_NO=f.CIF_NO
 LEFT JOIN BANK_DEMO.BIZ.SECTOR_MAP s ON s.NAICS_CD=c.NAICS_CD AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN s.EFF_FROM AND s.EFF_TO
 WHERE f.PRODUCT_CD='RLOC' AND f.FACILITY_STATUS='ACTIVE' AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN '2026-04-30' AND '2026-09-30'),
cohort AS (SELECT FACILITY_ID FROM base GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT SNAP_DT)=6)
SELECT sector, SNAP_DT, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(SUM(COMMIT_AMT)/1e6,1) commit_mm, ROUND(SUM(DRAWN_AMT)/1e6,1) drawn_mm,
 ROUND(100*SUM(DRAWN_AMT)/NULLIF(SUM(COMMIT_AMT),0),1) util_pct,
 ROUND(100*SUM(CASE WHEN FACILITY_ID IN (SELECT FACILITY_ID FROM cohort) THEN DRAWN_AMT END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN FACILITY_ID IN (SELECT FACILITY_ID FROM cohort) THEN COMMIT_AMT END),0),1) same_store_util_pct
FROM base GROUP BY ROLLUP(sector), SNAP_DT ORDER BY sector NULLS FIRST, SNAP_DT

WITH u AS (
 SELECT s.SECTOR, f.FACILITY_ID,
  MAX(CASE WHEN b.SNAP_DT='2026-04-30' THEN b.DRAWN_AMT/f.COMMIT_AMT END) u_apr,
  MAX(CASE WHEN b.SNAP_DT='2026-09-30' THEN b.DRAWN_AMT/f.COMMIT_AMT END) u_sep
 FROM BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY b
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY f ON f.FACILITY_ID=b.FACILITY_ID
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.CORE.CLIENT c ON c.CIF_NO=f.CIF_NO
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.BIZ.SECTOR_MAP s ON s.NAICS_CD=c.NAICS_CD AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN s.EFF_FROM AND s.EFF_TO
 WHERE f.PRODUCT_CD='RLOC' AND f.FACILITY_STATUS='ACTIVE' AND b.SNAP_DT IN ('2026-04-30','2026-09-30')
 GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT SECTOR, COUNT(*) n_both, SUM(IFF(u_sep-u_apr>0.10,1,0)) up_gt10pts, SUM(IFF(u_sep-u_apr<-0.10,1,0)) down_gt10pts,

text:
Revolving-line utilization across the portfolio rose from 47.1% in April to 49.8% in September 2026, up 2.7 points. Almost all of that came from two sectors: **Manufacturing** and **Wholesale Distribution**. In both, utilization climbed steadily by about 3.5 points every month for six months. Every other sector stayed flat at about 46%.

**Revolver utilization by sector (drawn ÷ commitment, month end)**

| Sector | Apr-26 | May | Jun | Jul | Aug | Sep-26 | Change (pts) | Sep drawn / commitment ($M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Manufacturing** | 51.6% | 55.1% | 58.6% | 62.1% | 65.6% | **69.1%** | **+17.5** | 366.6 / 530.9 |
| **Wholesale Distribution** | 51.0% | 54.5% | 58.0% | 61.5% | 65.1% | **68.6%** | **+17.6** | 230.9 / 336.8 |
| CRE Multifamily | 44.5% | 45.0% | 44.3% | 45.8% | 45.3% | 46.2% | +1.7 | 19.1 / 41.4 |
| Healthcare Services | 46.1% | 45.9% | 45.9% | 45.8% | 45.8% | 46.4% | +0.3 | 218.8 / 471.3 |
| Holding & Financial Cos. | 46.2% | 46.3% | 46.2% | 46.2% | 46.4% | 46.4% | +0.2 | 559.7 / 1,206.2 |
| Energy | 45.6% | 45.3% | 45.9% | 46.0% | 46.2% | 45.8% | +0.2 | 124.9 / 272.4 |
| Technology | 46.2% | 46.6% | 46.7% | 46.1% | 46.4% | 46.3% | +0.1 | 232.6 / 502.4 |
| Transportation & Logistics | 46.2% | 46.4% | 46.4% | 46.1% | 46.5% | 46.2% | 0.0 | 192.6 / 417.3 |
| Retail | 46.2% | 46.1% | 45.9% | 46.0% | 46.6% | 46.2% | 0.0 | 105.9 / 229.3 |
| Professional Services | 46.5% | 46.3% | 46.1% | 46.6% | 46.3% | 46.3% | −0.2 | 146.7 / 316.8 |
| Public & Not-for-Profit | 46.6% | 46.8% | 46.5% | 46.7% | 46.4% | 46.4% | −0.2 | 404.0 / 869.8 |
| CRE Office | 46.6% | 46.6% | 46.6% | 46.4% | 46.0% | 46.1% | −0.5 | 154.8 / 335.5 |
| **Total** | 47.1% | 47.7% | 48.3% | 48.8% | 49.4% | **49.8%** | **+2.7** | 2,756.6 / 5,530.0 |

**Where it's rising and what it means**
- **The rise is real, not caused by new lines.** I recalculated the trend using only the lines that existed in all six months, which removes the effect of lines booked in July–September. The results barely changed: Manufacturing still reaches 69.1% and Wholesale Distribution 68.5%. The portfolio total moves from 47.1% to 50.0%.
- **It's happening on every line in both sectors, not a few large borrowers.** All 65 Manufacturing lines and all 44 Wholesale Distribution lines that existed in both April and September rose by more than 10 points. The typical line in each rose 17.5 points. No line in any other sector rose more than 10 points.
- **No line is near its limit yet.** No line in any sector is at or above 80% utilization. But at about 3.5 points a month, both sectors' averages would cross 80% in roughly three months if the trend continues.
- **These two sectors account for the rise in total drawn balances.** Total drawn rose about $402M. Manufacturing (+$115M) and Wholesale Distribution (+$64M) make up about 45% of that, even though they hold only about 15% of commitments. Most of the rest comes from new lines in other sectors, which are drawing at about 46%.
- **Suggested next steps:** this pattern (both sectors rising together every month) often points to working-capital strain, such as inventory build-up or customers paying more slowly. It would be worth looking at these borrowers' days-past-due, risk-rating moves and covenant headroom, and their borrowing-base reporting where relevant.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Metric:** the knowledge layer's approved revolver-utilization definition: total drawn balance ÷ total commitment for active revolving lines (product code `RLOC`), at each month end.
- **Tables:**
  - `BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY` for drawn balances at each month end.
  - `BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY` for commitment, product and status.
  - `BANK_DEMO.CORE.CLIENT` for each borrower's industry code (NAICS).
  - `BANK_DEMO.BIZ.SECTOR_MAP` for the bank's sector groupings.
- **Sector mapping:** I used the approved client-to-sector join. The sector groups are the bank's own, not standard 2-digit NAICS groups. I applied the map's effective dates. Every code has one current entry and every line mapped to a sector.
- **Policy:** I used no restricted tables. RM production goals weren't needed.

**Assumptions**
- I followed the approved definition, so only lines that are active today are included in every month. About 2–6 lines a month that were later paid off are left out of the earlier months (about $12–31M of commitments, under 1% of the total). This doesn't change the trends.
- Commitment is the current committed amount on each line. Here it equals drawn plus undrawn in every month, so there's no difference from using the month-end balances.

sql.sql: SELECT NAICS_CD, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT SECTOR) ns, MIN(EFF_FROM), MAX(EFF_TO), LISTAGG(SECTOR||':'||EFF_FROM||'-'||COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(EFF_TO),'null'),' | ') FROM BANK_DEMO.BIZ.SECTOR_MAP GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 50

SELECT b.SNAP_DT, f.FACILITY_STATUS, COUNT(*) n, SUM(b.DRAWN_AMT) drawn, SUM(f.COMMIT_AMT) commit, SUM(b.DRAWN_AMT+b.UNDRAWN_AMT) bal_commit FROM BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY b JOIN BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY f ON f.FACILITY_ID=b.FACILITY_ID WHERE f.PRODUCT_CD='RLOC' AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-09-30' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

WITH base AS (
 SELECT COALESCE(s.SECTOR,'Unmapped') sector, b.SNAP_DT, b.FACILITY_ID, b.DRAWN_AMT, f.COMMIT_AMT
 FROM BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY b
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY f ON f.FACILITY_ID=b.FACILITY_ID
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.CORE.CLIENT c ON c.CIF_NO=f.CIF_NO
 LEFT JOIN BANK_DEMO.BIZ.SECTOR_MAP s ON s.NAICS_CD=c.NAICS_CD AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN s.EFF_FROM AND s.EFF_TO
 WHERE f.PRODUCT_CD='RLOC' AND f.FACILITY_STATUS='ACTIVE' AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN '2026-04-30' AND '2026-09-30'),
cohort AS (SELECT FACILITY_ID, 1 AS in_c FROM base GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT SNAP_DT)=6),
x AS (SELECT b.*, COALESCE(c.in_c,0) in_c FROM base b LEFT JOIN cohort c ON c.FACILITY_ID=b.FACILITY_ID)
SELECT COALESCE(sector,'TOTAL') sector, SNAP_DT, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(SUM(COMMIT_AMT)/1e6,1) commit_mm, ROUND(SUM(DRAWN_AMT)/1e6,1) drawn_mm,
 ROUND(100*SUM(DRAWN_AMT)/NULLIF(SUM(COMMIT_AMT),0),1) util_pct,
 ROUND(100*SUM(DRAWN_AMT*in_c)/NULLIF(SUM(COMMIT_AMT*in_c),0),1) same_store_util_pct
FROM x GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((sector, SNAP_DT),(SNAP_DT)) ORDER BY 1, 2

WITH u AS (
 SELECT s.SECTOR, f.FACILITY_ID,
  MAX(CASE WHEN b.SNAP_DT='2026-04-30' THEN b.DRAWN_AMT/f.COMMIT_AMT END) u_apr,
  MAX(CASE WHEN b.SNAP_DT='2026-09-30' THEN b.DRAWN_AMT/f.COMMIT_AMT END) u_sep
 FROM BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY b
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.LENDING.FACILITY f ON f.FACILITY_ID=b.FACILITY_ID
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.CORE.CLIENT c ON c.CIF_NO=f.CIF_NO
 JOIN BANK_DEMO.BIZ.SECTOR_MAP s ON s.NAICS_CD=c.NAICS_CD AND b.SNAP_DT BETWEEN s.EFF_FROM AND s.EFF_TO
 WHERE f.PRODUCT_CD='RLOC' AND f.FACILITY_STATUS='ACTIVE' AND b.SNAP_DT IN ('2026-04-30','2026-09-30')
 GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT SECTOR, COUNT(*) n_both, SUM(IFF(u_sep-u_apr>0.10,1,0)) up_gt10pts, SUM(IFF(u_sep-u_apr<-0.10,1,0)) down_gt10pts,
 ROUND(100*MEDIAN(u_sep-u_apr),1) median_chg_pts, SUM(IFF(u_sep>=0.80,1,0)) n_sep_ge80, SUM(IFF(u_apr>=0.80,1,0)) n_apr_ge80
FROM u WHERE u_apr IS NOT NULL AND u_sep IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY median_chg_pts DESC

MATCH (d:DecisionTrace {id: $id}) UNWIND $names AS nm
                  CALL (nm) {
                    MATCH (n) WHERE (n:Concept OR n:DataProduct OR n:Metric OR n:JoinPath OR n:Policy OR n:Report OR n:BusinessRule)
                      AND (toLower(n.name) = toLower(nm) OR n.id = nm OR toLower(n.id) = toLower(nm))
                    RETURN n LIMIT 1
                    UNION
                    MATCH (n:Table) WHERE toUpper(n.fq_name) = toUpper(nm) OR toUpper(n.fq_name) ENDS WITH '.' + toUpper(nm)
                    RETURN n LIMIT 1 }
                  MERGE (d)-[:USED]->(n) RETURN collect(DISTINCT coalesce(n.fq_name, n.name, n.id)) AS linked

MATCH (d:DecisionTrace {id: $id}) UNWIND $ids AS eid
                 MATCH (n:LegalEntity) WHERE n.id = eid
                 MERGE (d)-[:ABOUT]->(n) RETURN collect(DISTINCT n.id) AS about

MATCH (d:DecisionTrace {id: $id}) UNWIND $checks AS c
                   MATCH (p:Policy {id: c.policy})
                   MERGE (d)-[r:CHECKED]->(p) SET r.decision = c.decision RETURN collect(p.id + ':' + c.decision) AS checked
